newsitem.title: USA: Starbucks sets sights on Florida.
newsitem.headline: Starbucks sets sights on Florida.

text.p: Starbucks Corp. said Friday it is confident it can sell its upscale coffee in Miami, although the city of hot sun, beaches and cool drinks is a far cry from the company's cloudy, chilly Seattle base.
"People drink coffee everywhere," Starbucks zone Vice President Marcia Adams said.
The company recently opened two stores in the Miami suburbs and a third will open soon.
Adams said the company's current plan was to open 13 stand-alone stores in Florida, all in Dade, Broward and Palm Beach counties by the end of September.
"Florida has a very high coffee consumption rate compared with the rest of the country," she said.

Adams would not project sales figures, but said Starbucks did not anticipate problems winning an audience in Miami, although she acknowledged the area is known best for "cafe cubano," thimble-sized plastic cups of sugar-sweetened espresso brought to Florida by the Cuban-American community.

The company opted not to translate its signs into Spanish -- the native tongue of an estimated 60 percent of people in the Miami area -- although about half the staff hired in the region speak the language.

"We talked about it and we really felt we needed to come into the market as a true Starbucks," she said. She said Starbucks had done a strong mail-order business in the region even before it decided to open stores here.
Starbucks currently has about 1,100 stores nationwide.
